note: The listening set of the voice comparison as it goes onto the audition page: the four lines marked 'listen' in lines.json, each spoken by the five models, grouped by line so that the owner compares the models on the same sentence. Every file is the dry speech: lines of the role 'radio' get the path 'radio', so the page plays them through its radio filter (the switch 'Funkfilter' turns it off). tools/voice/publish.py writes the files.

models.name: Qwen3-TTS
models.licence: speech generated with Qwen3-TTS (code and weights Apache-2.0)
models.about: Model: Qwen3-TTS. The voice was built from a text description and is no person's voice. This is the reference for quality; with the package as it is, it speaks slower than real time even on the graphics card, so it suits lines made ahead, not live speech.

models.name: Chatterbox-Nano
models.licence: speech generated with Chatterbox-Nano (code and weights MIT), in the voice of a clip made by Qwen3-TTS
models.about: Model: Chatterbox-Nano. It speaks in the same designed voice as the Qwen3 sample (it copies that clip). It runs on a processor without a graphics card, somewhat faster than real time. It embeds an inaudible watermark.

models.name: Kokoro
models.licence: speech generated with Kokoro-82M (code and weights Apache-2.0); the voice is a blend of preset voices whose origin the makers do not document
models.about: Model: Kokoro-82M. Small and fast, on a processor several times faster than real time, and it can run in a browser. The voice is a blend of the model's preset voices; where those come from is not documented.

models.name: Kitten TTS 2 Mini
models.licence: speech generated with Kitten TTS 2 Mini (code, weights and voice packs Apache-2.0); a preset voice whose origin the makers do not state
models.about: Model: Kitten TTS 2 Mini, the smallest of the five. Fast on a processor. The voice is one of the model's presets; the makers do not say where it comes from.

models.name: Phonon 31M
models.licence: speech generated with Phonon 31M (weights and voices Apache-2.0); a character voice the makers state was made by voice design
models.about: Model: Phonon 31M. It runs inside a browser tab (a 65 MB file) and is the fastest. The voice is one of the makers' designed fantasy characters, the nearest there was, so it does not fit the role: listen to how it speaks, not to who speaks.

composed.note: Composed files that are listed after the lines above, as further entries of the category: not cut or trimmed by publish.py (the file keeps its silence up to the moment of the jump), made by tools/voice/countdown.py. 'intent' of the manifest is the line, then 'how', then 'about'.

entries.de: Countdown im Sekundentakt · Qwen3-TTS, Zahlen einzeln gesprochen
entries.en: Countdown on a one-second grid · Qwen3-TTS, numbers spoken one by one
entries.how: the five numbers were spoken one by one as separate utterances (several takes of each; the take of each was chosen by measurement: the recogniser reads it back as the number, the sounding part is 0.2 to 0.8 s long, level near the others, most similar to the speaker of the intro)

entries.en: Countdown on a one-second grid · Qwen3-TTS, numbers cut out of one sentence
entries.how: the whole line was spoken as one utterance and the five numbers were cut out of it at the word boundaries (Whisper word time stamps, refined to the level minimum between two words, each cut word read back by the recogniser)
